name: fullstack-typescript-platform
description: Auth, RBAC, REST + GraphQL and WebSockets over one domain layer, in TypeScript. Postgres, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes manifests.
author: Nur Afzan Zulaikha
comment:layout: This is a task runner, not an npm workspace root. `server` and `web` are two independent
applications that happen to share a repository: they share no code, they talk to each other
over HTTP, and each has its own lockfile, its own Dockerfile and its own CI job.
It DID declare `workspaces: [server, web]`, and CI proved that wrong immediately. With a
workspace root present, npm treats the root as the project and looks for the lockfile there,
so `npm ci` inside server/ failed with EUSAGE: 'can only install with an existing
package-lock.json'. The per-package lockfiles were still on disk; npm had simply stopped
Hoisting to a root lockfile was the alternative, but it makes both Dockerfiles worse: each
builds from its own directory as context, and a root lockfile would force a repo-root build
context plus a workspace-scoped install just to reach it. Two independent packages is what
the deployment topology already is, so the manifest now says so.

scripts.install:all: cd server && npm ci && cd ../web && npm ci
scripts.typecheck: cd server && npm run typecheck && cd ../web && npm run typecheck
scripts.test: cd server && npm test && cd ../web && npm test
scripts.test:coverage: cd server && npm run test:coverage && cd ../web && npm run test:coverage
scripts.build: cd server && npm run build && cd ../web && npm run build
